title: Value of an Asana OAuth refresh token in a token response or refresh request
summary: A synthetic value of the refresh_token member of a pretty-printed token exchange response, and of the refresh_token parameter in a raw form-encoded refresh request and a curl --data-urlencode argument.
rationale: The carrier is documented: the token exchange response carries the refresh token in its refresh_token member, and a refresh request passes it as the refresh_token parameter of a form-encoded POST body with grant_type refresh_token. Asana states no prefix, alphabet or length and says tokens are opaque, so the value is flagged because of where it sits, not because of its shape. The extent is the value only: the member or parameter name, the colon or equals sign, the ampersand and the quotes are outside it, and the client_id beside it is a public identifier.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the string value of the refresh_token member of a token exchange response, or of the refresh_token parameter of a refresh request, is treated as a credential whatever its shape. Asana documents the refresh_token response member and the refresh_token request parameter (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic attribution are the project's decisions. No subtype is inferred, and no prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: If exchanging a `code`, this is a long-lived token that can be used to get new access tokens when older ones expire
If the value of grant_type is refresh_token, this is the refresh token you are using to be granted a new access token

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
